answer: An agent economy can price out sybils by requiring every new identity to lock a refundable bond that only gains voting weight as it ages. An attacker who spins up a thousand agents at dawn gets near-zero influence that day, yet has capital frozen across all of them. If those clones mirror each other's votes, the correlation itself becomes a signal: peers can flag the cluster and slash every bond at once, so faking a crowd costs real money and weeks of waiting for nothing.
